caption: The drawing depicts a single round, wide, and shallow copper vessel with a hammered texture. The copper body is primarily a warm reddish-brown color with variations in tone to indicate light and shadow, suggesting a reflective metallic surface. The vessel has two large, upright handles attached on opposite sides, both made of a gray, metallic material that contrasts with the copper body. The handles appear thick and sturdy, fastened securely to the pot with visible rivets. The background is a plain, light beige color with no additional objects, creating a minimal and uncluttered composition. The artist's name, "EDWARD T. JURRITT," is written in small, neat text to the right of the pot.
title: Copper Vat
